c.n: The Loire is France’s white-wine river.
c.s: The Loire is France’s white-wine river.

c.n: It runs about 600 miles across France to
c.s: It runs about 600 miles across France to the Atlantic. Near the coast the weather is mild and maritime. Inland it turns continental: warmer summers, colder winters. White is the main color, and each stop on the river leans on its own grape.

c.n: Muscadet is a dry white from Melon B, of
c.s: Muscadet is a dry white from Melon B, often aged on its yeast (sur lie). Bracing and citrusy: a seafood wine.

c.n: Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc country.
c.s: Chenin Blanc and Cabernet Franc country. Savennières is dry Chenin. Quarts de Chaume and Bonnezeaux are sweet Chenin from noble rot.

c.n: Vouvray is Chenin Blanc, made dry, sweet
c.s: Vouvray is Chenin Blanc, made dry, sweet or sparkling. Chinon and Bourgueil are Cabernet Franc reds.
Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé are Sauvignon Blanc. Sancerre also makes red and rosé from Pinot Noir.
